body_ar:
الصفات الفعلية الثابتة لله تعالى منها ما اشتق منه اسم الله تعالى، ومنها ما ليست كذلك، وقد أثبت الله لنفسه في كتابه وأثبت له رسوله صفات كثيرة، وقد ذكر الشيخ هنا بعضها وشرحها.
بعض صفات الله الفعلية:
قال الشيخ: [يسمع يبصر يحب يعجب يضحك يرضى يستجيب يغضب] هذا البيت كله يتضمن ثماني صفات من صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى الفعلية، بعض هذه الصفات مقتضية أيضاً لبعض الأسماء من أسمائه، فمثلاً: ......
إثبات صفة السمع لله عز وجل:
قوله: (يسمع): هذا إثبات لصفة السمع لله سبحانه وتعالى، والله تعالى يقول: قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَا [المجادلة:1] فهذا إثبات لهذه الصفة الفعلية، وهو إثبات أيضاً لاسم (السميع) فهو اسم مشتق من هذه الصفة. وسمع الله سبحانه وتعالى الراجح أنه للأصوات أي: يتعلق بالأصوات، وأنه لا يتعلق بالذوات، وخالف في هذا المتكلمون، فإنهم يقولون: سمعه يتعلق بالذوات والأصوات، وبصره يتعلق بالذوات والمبصرات، وليس لهم على هذا أي دليل...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Among the active attributes established for God, exalted is He, there are some from which a name of God, exalted is He, is derived, and some that are not so. God has affirmed for Himself in His Book, and His Messenger has affirmed for Him, a great many attributes; the Sheikh mentions some of them here and explains them.

## Some of God's active attributes

The Sheikh said:

*[He hears, He sees, He loves, He wonders, He laughs, He is pleased, He answers, He is angry.]*

This whole line contains eight of the active attributes of God, glorified and exalted is He. Some of these attributes also require certain of His names. For example: ……

## Affirming the attribute of hearing for God, mighty and majestic

His words "He hears": this is an affirmation of the attribute of hearing for God, glorified and exalted is He. God, exalted is He, says: {God has indeed heard the words of her who disputes with you concerning her husband and complains to God, and God hears the two of you conversing} (Sūrat al-Mujādalah 58:1). This is an affirmation of this active attribute, and it is an affirmation also of the name "the All-Hearing" (al-Samīʿ), which is a name derived from this attribute.

As for the hearing of God, glorified and exalted is He, the stronger position is that it is of sounds — that is, that it attaches to sounds and does not attach to entities. The theologians of kalām dissented on this, for they say: His hearing attaches to entities and to sounds, and His sight attaches to entities and to visible things. And they have no evidence whatever for this…

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

This record does carry a CMS timestamp in a .create_date span (10 May 2011, within a 28-minute window shared by the whole run 738-747). That is a bulk-upload timestamp for the series, not the date the lesson was given, and it is not evidence of composition date. Record 737, translated in an earlier wave, reports no date for this run; the timestamp is in fact present in the page and should be backfilled there.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
Creedal material. Per style guide section 8, the vocabulary of divine attributes is not the vocabulary of the five legal rulings and the five-rulings mapping is not applied anywhere in this record.

Eight attributes are listed in the quoted line and only the first is expounded before the record stops. Marked critical_for_display: seven attributes are named here with no explanation whatever, and the rejection of the mutakallimūn's position ('they have no evidence whatever for this') is the last thing on the page, with whatever qualification followed it sitting in the .doc.

'المتكلمون' is rendered 'the theologians of kalām' rather than 'the theologians', so that the reference to a particular discipline and its practitioners is not read as a statement about theologians in general.
